title: Engineer Influence: Pocket Toolkit (Draft)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Engineer Influence: Pocket Toolkit — quick deck for SEs and sellers to engage platform & infra engineers
Speaker note: one-slide elevator: what an engineer wants — clarity on latency/cost, migration steps, rollback safety. keep it technical and concise.

Slide 2 — Why this matters to engineers
- Engineers care about predictability: 'How will this affect p99 latency and tail variance?'
- They care about economics: 'Is this predictable per-request cost at scale?'
- They care about risk: 'Can we fallback gracefully and audit requests?'
- They care about ownership: 'How much infra and ops do we need to run?'

Speaker note: convert sales language to engineer-first language. Avoid marketing fluff.

Slide 3 — Core technical narrative (30s)
- Redwood provides a single runtime API and deploy model across hosted, dedicated, and private modes.
- For platform teams: same API surface, same routing logic, consistent tracing and cost signals.
- Short pitch line: 'One control plane, multiple safety valves'

Slide 4 — Quick architecture sketch (visual notes)
- Box 1: Client app -> Box 2: Redwood control plane (routing/policy) -> Box 3a: Hosted model pool / 3b: Dedicated pool / 3c: Private VPC nodes
- Side services: telemetry, KV prefix cache, rollout manager, key-manager/HSM
Visual cue: highlight 'fallbacks' arrows between 3a->3b->3c and region failover paths.

Slide 5 — Common engineer objections & micro-responses (use as cheat cards)
Objection: 'We can self-host — why Redwood?'
- Micro-response: focus on lifecycle: "We handle optimized kernels, KV cache orchestration, autoscaling, and continuous batching out-of-box — you keep the service code, we run the heavy inference plumbing."

Objection: 'I need on-prem for compliance'
- Micro-response: "Private deployment with a customer-managed control plane, optional air-gapped package, and KMS/HSM integrations. We provide migration steps and preflight checklists."

Objection: 'Latency will be unpredictable'
- Micro-response: "Per-route SLOs, token-level latency breakdown, and live tracing. We also support pinned model versions and immediate canary rollouts to reduce risk."

Objection: 'We can't accept model outputs blindly'
- Micro-response: "Function/tool calling, structured output enforcement and post-processing hooks + eval integration for regressions."

Slide 6 — POC checklist (engineer-focused)
Goal: validate latency, cost, and fallback logic in 2 weeks
1) Baseline: run current inference calls against 1000 synthetic requests (same prompt distribution). capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
2) Redwood hosted endpoint: run same load, capture metrics.
3) Dedicated pool preview (if available): compare throughput scaling; toggle batch sizes and observe tail latency.
4) Simulate an outage: configure routing policy to failover to secondary model variant and measure degraded latency and correctness.
5) Security audit: validate VPC peering and KMS with a sample encryption key and confirm audit log entries.
6) Developer ergonomics: time-to-first-call using SDKs (JS/Python) and sample curl snippets.

Speaker note: include an appendix with curl snippets and sample configs. keep checklist in bullet form for quick handoff.

Slide 7 — Demo snippets (copy-paste ready)
- cURL (simple sync call):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY'
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
    -d '{"model":"rwd-gpt-3.8", "input":"Summarize the following..."}'

- JS (streaming):
  // pseudo-code
  const client = new Redwood({key: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY});
  const stream = client.chat.stream({model: 'rwd-chat-3.8', messages});
  for await (const chunk of stream) console.log(chunk);

Slide 8 — Fallback & rollback playbook (engineer checklist)
- Canary: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% with metrics gate on p99 and correctness tests
- Auto-fallback: policy to route to quantized model or cached responses on latency breach
- Emergency rollback: config flag in control plane to pin previous model and disable advanced batching
- Post-incident: add failing prompts to regression suite, trigger Optimize recommendations for quantization/batching adjustments.

Slide 9 — Cost vs latency knobs (engineer cheat)
- Batching window: increase to reduce cost at expense of tail latency
- KV prefix caching: fastest for repeated prefixes (e.g., chat contexts)
- Quantization profile: 8-bit vs 4-bit tradeoffs; recommend running eval test with typical prompts
- Model routing: prefer smaller model for high-throughput, heavy-tail lower-latency spores go to dedicated/pinned nodes

Slide 10 — Suggested trial plan for platform teams (2-week sprint)
Week 0: kickoff, access keys, preflight network test
Week 1: baseline runs + hosted POC + basic canary
Week 2: dedicated trials or private trial + security validation + handoff doc
Deliverable: one-pager with p99 latency delta, cost delta per 10k requests, and recommended deployment mode.

Slide 11 — Success signals (what to measure)
- p99 latency delta <= +25% compared to baseline for same throughput (target depends on use case)
- Cost per request reduction >= 10% (for chat-heavy workloads)
- Failure recovery time < 60s with auto-fallback in place
- Developer time-to-first-call < 30 minutes (SDK/curl)

Slide 12 — Appendix: evaluation prompts to detect regressions
- List of ~30 prompts covering: short answers, long-form summarization, tabular extraction, multi-turn context, hallucination stressors
- Example: "Given invoice text, extract date, vendor, total, and line items as JSON"

Slide 13 — Talking scripts (30s snippets)
- For platform eng: 'We can run a short two-week proof to measure p99 and cost at your scale; if it doesn't meet the gate, you keep your current stack — no lock-in.'
- For infra/security: 'We provide private control plane options and KMS/HSM integrations; we can run a preflight network scan together.'

Slide 14 — Open questions / TODOs for internal alignment
- Need official telemetry sample dashboards to share with customers (ask observability team)
- Create a small repo with reproducible POC harness (benchmark scripts + prompts)
- Get legal quick checklist for air-gapped trial agreements

Slide 15 — Quick resources & links
- Internal repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sales-demos/engineer-toolkit
- Confluence: ENG-ONBOARD-4921 (POC runbook)
- Demo ticket: JIRA-GTM-882

Notes to self: keep deck short (10–12 slides), include at least one simple graph from a real run (p50/p99 table), and a screenshot of the console rollout UI. Avoid marketing buzz; keep all bullets engineer-focused and operational.
